leads.title: Regulate Experimental Adolescent Procedures (REAP) Act
leads.documents: State ban on gender-affirming care for individuals under age 18; Mississippi became 3rd state to enact such ban in 2023 after Utah and South Dakota
leads.detail: Signed Feb 28, 2023 by Governor Tate Reeves; passed by both chambers earlier that month; led to closure of UMMC TEAM Clinic June 30, 2023

leads.title: Mississippi SB 2536 (2021) - Transgender Sports Ban
leads.documents: Bans transgender athletes from participating in sports teams or Olympic events corresponding with gender identity; requires physician statement verifying genitalia, DNA, hormone levels if sex disputed
leads.detail: Senate 34-9, House 81-28; signed by Gov. Tate Reeves March 11, 2021; effective July 1

leads.title: 2024 Public School Bathroom Law
leads.documents: Requires individuals in public schools to use bathrooms consistent with sex 'determined solely by birth'
leads.detail: Passed by Mississippi Legislature early May 2024; signed May 13, 2024 by Gov. Tate Reeves; took effect immediately

leads.title: Religious Liberty Accommodations Act - HB 1523 (2016)
leads.documents: Protects individuals, religious organizations, some businesses acting on beliefs that marriage is one man-one woman, sexual relations confined to such marriage, gender determined at birth; enables refusal of services
leads.detail: Scheduled effective July 1, 2016; enjoined June 30 by U.S. District Judge Carlton W. Reeves; injunction lifted June 23, 2017 by Fifth Circuit for lack of standing; guided by Alliance Defending Freedom

leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County, 590 U.S. (2020)
leads.documents: U.S. Supreme Court holding that workplace discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity is discrimination based on sex under Title VII of Civil Rights Act of 1964
leads.detail: Decided June 15, 2020; consolidated with Altitude Express v. Zarda and R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes v. EEOC; provides federal employment protection despite no state law

leads.title: Campaign for Southern Equality v. Bryant / Obergefell v. Hodges
leads.documents: Invalidation of Mississippi same-sex marriage ban; nationwide recognition of same-sex marriage
leads.detail: District Judge Carlton W. Reeves ruled Mississippi ban unconstitutional Nov 25, 2014 with 2-week stay extended Dec 4 by Fifth Circuit; U.S. Supreme Court Obergefell decided June 26, 2015; AG Jim Hood directed compliance June 29

leads.title: Federal Adoption Ban Ruling - U.S. District Judge Daniel Porter Jordan III
leads.documents: Striking down Mississippi's 2000 law banning adoption and fostering by same-sex couples; Mississippi was last state with such ban
leads.detail: Lawsuit filed Aug 12, 2015 by Campaign for Southern Equality, Family Equality Council and four couples; preliminary injunction March 31, 2016; final May 2, 2016, no appeal

leads.title: Mississippi Identity Documents Rules - Supreme Court Name-Change Ruling and Driver's License Law
leads.documents: Limits on transgender name and gender-marker changes: teen cannot change name until 21 for 'lack of maturity'; driver's licenses must reflect sex assigned at birth
leads.detail: Supreme Court ruling April 2025 misgendering teen despite parental support; Vital Records requires court order + medical statement; Gender Designation Form allowed Nov 1, 2021-March 2026; new prohibitive law passed March 2026; Real You Act introduced Jan 17, 2022 by Sen. Chad McMahan died Feb 2022

leads.title: Mississippi Hate Crime Statute (1994) and Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act (2009) - U.S. v. Joshua Vallum (2017)
leads.documents: State hate-crime law excludes sexual orientation/gender identity; federal law covers both allowing federal prosecution in Mississippi; first federal prosecution was Mississippi transgender murder
leads.detail: State law covers race, color, ancestry, ethnicity, religion, national origin, disability only; federal Act signed 2009 by President Obama; Vallum sentenced to 49 years federal prison for murdering transgender former girlfriend

leads.title: Williams Institute 2024 HIV Criminalization Report and The Trevor Project 2024 Survey
leads.documents: Institutional data on enforcement and human-rights conditions: HIV arrests and LGBTQ youth conversion-therapy exposure in Mississippi
leads.detail: Williams Institute found at least 43 arrested for HIV-related offenses 2004-2021 under felony non-disclosure law; Trevor Project found 8% of LGBTQ youth subjected to conversion therapy, 12% threatened; state HIV rate 17.8 per 100,000 vs 11.2 national
